correctness.rationale: The quotient of the 2n-vertex Möbius ladder by rotation 2m is a degree-L covering of the labelled graph B_m: spoke displacement mL reduces to m because L is odd. Full inverse images of edge sets are matchings iff the downstairs sets are matchings by the covering local star bijection. A perfect matching downstairs lifts; for the converse, deleting vertices of a proposed matching leaves a degree-L bipartite covering, and a large perfect matching gives nonnegative edge weights with incident sum L at each residual base vertex. The derived Hall inequalities force a downstairs perfect matching. Fixed barycentric coordinates are constant on each edge orbit and a complete orbit is a simplex exactly in this case; orbit barycenters give the claimed PL triangulation. m=1 retains three distinct labelled parallel edges. Agarwal–Basak Main Theorem 1 and Theorem 21 supply the cited nonequivariant sphere counts. Independently enumerated base perfect-matching face systems agree with full orbit systems at (m,L)=(1,3),(3,3),(3,5),(5,3).
